# Customer interview guide

A topic-by-topic question bank for a general customer-discovery interview — open-ended questions with real follow-up probes, drafted from your research goal and yours to edit before you take it into the room.

Family: Voice of the customer · Format: .xlsx · Domain: core

## What it is

An interview guide is what turns 'go talk to some customers' into a real, repeatable instrument — a topic-by-topic question bank built around a stated research goal, with genuine follow-up probes woven in, not just a list of first questions. State who you're talking to and what you're trying to learn; a full guide gets drafted, and it's yours to edit before you take it into the room.

## When to use it

Use it when:

- You're about to run a general discovery interview and want a real instrument, not an improvised conversation.
- You have a stated research goal — even a rough one — that a structured question bank would serve better than winging it.
- You want interview-technique reminders specific to this conversation, not generic interviewing advice.

Not when:

- The interview is happening in context, watching real work as it's done — that's the gemba interview protocol, built around what's observed in the moment rather than recalled afterward.
- The interview is specifically about a closed deal (won or lost) — that's the win-loss interview guide, built around a decision that's already been made.
- You don't have a real research goal yet, just a vague sense you should 'talk to customers more' — sharpen the goal first, or the guide will be as vague as the goal.

## How to fill it in

- **researchGoal** — What are you actually trying to learn? Specific beats broad — 'understand why onboarding takes longer than expected' drafts a sharper guide than 'understand the customer experience.'
- **topics** — Drafted from your research goal and any seed topics you already had in mind — add, remove, or reword anything before the interview.
- **reminders** — Drafted for this specific guide's context — real interview-technique discipline, not generic platitudes.
- **narrative** — Drafted from the research goal — how to actually run this conversation and what to listen for.

## What good looks like

The example below is a general onboarding-discovery guide: four topics building from background through to open frustrations, real follow-up probes within each topic, and interview-technique reminders grounded in the coaching stance this whole product tries to model — ask before answering, let silence sit.

Full worked example, on-screen and as a downloadable .xlsx: https://katafacts.com/katas/customer-interview-guide

## Common mistakes

- **Writing questions that are really statements looking for agreement.** — "Wasn't onboarding frustrating?" plants the answer before the customer has said anything — open-ended questions surface what's actually there, leading questions confirm what you already believe.
- **Treating the question list as a script to read verbatim rather than a guide to work from.** — The real value of an interview comes from the follow-up that isn't written down — a rigid script misses exactly the specific detail a genuine 'tell me more' would surface.
- **Covering too many topics to go deep on any of them.** — Same vital-few discipline as everywhere else in this catalogue — a focused guide that goes deep on three topics beats a shallow pass across eight.

## What it connects to

Downstream:

- **VOC evidence log** — The quotes and observations this interview produces are exactly what feeds the evidence log — log them as they come in, not from memory afterward.
- **Affinity diagram** — Once you've run several interviews, an affinity-diagramming session is where the individual quotes get synthesized into real themes.

## Where AI helps

Judgement — stays with you:

- Deciding whether a drafted question actually fits the real conversation, or reworking it before the interview
- Knowing when to deviate from the guide because something more interesting just came up

Analysis — AI helps:

- Drafting open-ended questions and real follow-up probes from a stated research goal
- Drafting interview-technique reminders specific to this guide's context

Drudgery — automated:

- Counting topics and questions
- Exporting to xlsx in the house format
